text:
Alex: thinking about the runtime adapter pattern for hosted/dedicated/private — we keep circling back to two options: 1) a single thin facade that delegates to env-specific adapters, or 2) explicit capability flags + translation layer per request. which direction avoids drift and keeps observability consistent?
Maria: +1 on doing a thin facade but worried about hidden semantics. what happens when private needs different auth/secret flows (HSM/KMS) and hosted uses api-keys?
Sam: the auth bit is a big one. if facade hides it, ops teams won't see per-env failures. maybe facade should be only routing; translation layer must be explicit and testable.
Alex: agree. propose: facade = routing + lightweight validation, adapters implement TranslateRequest(RequestV1)->EnvRequest with tests. keep common telemetry hooks in facade so traces look uniform.
PlatformBot: deploy-note: canary deployed adapter v0.3 to staging cluster at 2024-04-15T09:12Z :rocket:
Jordan: how do we version TranslateRequest? if adapters diverge we'll need compatibility guarantees. maybe require adapters to support a minimal API contract: Start(), Translate(), Drain(), Health().
Kevin: sketch of minimal interface:
```
interface Adapter {
  Start(ctx)
  Translate(req) -> {env_headers, env_body}
  Health() -> status
  Drain()
}
```
Maria: +1. also add a Metadata() call that returns which capabilities adapter supports (batching, kv-cache, quantized runtime hints). that way the facade can make routing decisions.
Sam: good call. we also need a capability discovery endpoint exposed to control-plane for billing and rollout rules. e.g., adapter reports {supports_prefetch: true, max_seq: 4096, cost_multiplier: 1.2}.
Alex: yes. cost_multiplier will be used for per-token billing attribution in dedicated vs hosted. must be auditable. logs + signed metadata from private adapters (customer KMS) for trust.
Jordan: question: who owns translation tests? infra or adapter authors? infra should provide a test harness that runs golden prompts and validates outputs across envs. adapters must pass.
Kevin: test harness should include simulated failure modes: slow KMS, partial KV cache miss, large-batch backpressure. add validators for latency SLOs and token accounting.
Maria: concerning secrets: private adapters may require access to customer HSMs — we can't replicate that in CI. propose we define a mock interface and require adapters to run in two modes: real-secret-mode (only in customer env) and mock-secret-mode (in CI) with the same call traces.
Sam: +1. also document the failure semantics explicitly: if secret call fails -> fail-fast or fallback to hosted? default should be fail-fast for security, but facade can apply fallback policy if customer configured fallback.
Alex: action items: 1) Jordan to draft Adapter API RFC with Metadata() and capability schema. 2) Kevin to prototype test harness with failure injections. 3) Maria to write secret-mode mock pattern + CI guidelines. 4) Sam to add billing metadata schema.
Jordan: I'll start RFC draft this week. initial appendix will include examples of Translate() mappings for streaming vs non-streaming, and a sample capability response: {"supports_streaming":true,"batching_model":"continuous","max_tokens":8192}.
PlatformBot: reminder: RFC templates repo updated: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs :link:
Kevin: one more design note — observability. facade must inject a canonical request_id and map adapter-specific spans back to it. append a small env-span header in Translate() output so traces correlate.
Maria: and add a structured metric for "adapter_cost_estimate" so optimizer can suggest quantization or routing changes automatically.
Alex: sounds good. try to keep adapter implementations small and opinionated. we want clear boundaries, not a swiss-army knife.
Jordan: ok filing RFC, will ping this thread when draft is ready.
Sam: thanks all. :thumbsup:
